guarantees.text: the value starts at `initialValue`, 0 when it is not given
`increment` adds `step` to the value, `decrement` subtracts it
the value never goes above `max` or below `min`
`set` sets the value to the given number, within `min` and `max`
`reset` sets the value back to `initialValue`
the state starts at `initialState`, false when it is not given
`open` sets the state to true, `close` to false, `toggle` to its opposite and `set` to the given value
`onOpen` is called when the state changes to true and `onClose` when it changes to false
`open` when already open and `close` when already closed do nothing and call no callback
returns one of "undetermined", "macos", "ios", "windows", "android", "linux" and "chromeos", according to the user agent
returns "undetermined" when the OS cannot be identified, for example during server-side rendering

params.name:
{
  total,
  siblings = 1,
  boundaries = 1,
  page,
  initialPage,
  onChange,
  startValue = 1,
}

guarantees.text: with total 10 and page 1, range is [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, "dots", 10]; on page 5 it is [1, "dots", 4, 5, 6, "dots", 10]; on page 6 [1, "dots", 5, 6, 7, "dots", 10]; on page 10 [1, "dots", 6, 7, 8, 9, 10]
`siblings` and `boundaries` default to 1, and the first page defaults to 1 or `startValue`
`next`, `previous`, `first` and `last` move the active page to the next, previous, first and last page
with `page` and `onChange`, `setPage` calls `onChange` with the page and the active page follows `page`
`siblings` sets how many pages are shown on each side of the active page
`boundaries` sets how many pages are shown at each edge
with `startValue` 5 and `total` 15, the pages range from 5 to 15
`initialValues` (default empty) are divided between state and queue: the first `limit` items in state, the rest in queue
`add` puts items in state while state holds fewer than `limit` items, and in queue after that
`update` applies the function to all items of state and queue, then divides the result again by `limit`, keeping order
`cleanQueue` empties the queue and leaves state unchanged
the value starts at the first element of `options`
calling the toggle function with no argument moves the value to the next element of `options`, and from the last back to the first (["light", "dark"]: "dark", then "light")
calling the toggle function with a value sets the value to it
without `options`, the value starts at false and toggles between false and true
